discovery: Discovery of gamma-ray burst afterglows and the cosmological origin of gamma-ray bursts

nominees.name: Enrico Costa
nominees.affiliation: INAF - Istituto di Astrofisica e Planetologia Spaziali, Rome, Italy

motivation: For 25 years, gamma-ray bursts were the deepest mystery in high-energy astrophysics. In 1997 Costa and Frontera used the BeppoSAX wide-field and narrow-field X-ray instruments, which they helped design, to discover the fading X-ray afterglow of GRB 970228. This gave arcminute positions within hours, which had never been possible before. Kulkarni and colleagues then used these positions to find optical and radio counterparts and to measure the first redshifts, which placed bursts at cosmological distances. Radio scintillation showed that the emitting source was expanding relativistically. Together these results showed that bursts are the most luminous explosions in the universe, from the collapse of massive stars and from compact-object mergers. They created the afterglow field, including the discovery that GRB jets are collimated. They led to Swift, and they made possible the 2017 kilonova counterpart to a gravitational-wave source. This is a classic case of a new instrumental capability transforming physical understanding.
